classification.difficultyReason: Introduce an unshown perpendicular from the apex and use isosceles symmetry to halve the base. Then identify adjacent side and hypotenuse and apply inverse cosine.

content.prompt: Find the base angle in the isosceles triangle, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: An unshaded isosceles triangle with a horizontal base, matching single ticks on its sloping sides and beta at the left base angle. Decorative blue source outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Both sloping sides are 7 cm; the base is 10 cm. Coordinates use altitude sqrt(24), preserving the stated lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no altitude, half-base measurement or calculated angle is supplied.

answer.short:
$\beta\approx44.42^\circ$.

Draw the perpendicular from the apex to halve the base, then use cosine.
answer.worked:
Draw a perpendicular from the apex to the base. In an isosceles triangle, this bisects the base, giving a right-angled triangle with adjacent side $5\text{ cm}$ and hypotenuse $7\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}\cos\beta&=\frac{5}{7}\\\beta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{7}\right)\\\beta&\approx44.42^\circ\end{align*}$$
